arguments: Failed encrypt/decrypt setup may release using an uninitialized or caller-seeded handle value
message.text: Failed encrypt/decrypt setup may release using an uninitialized or caller-seeded handle value

properties.metisTriageReason: Verdict: The reported release of an uninitialized or caller-seeded handle is contradicted by the allocation contract. Evidence: setup seeds `*p_handle` from `iov->op_handle` before calling `tfm_crypto_operation_alloc`, but allocation rejects any non-invalid input handle and on success writes the allocated handle before returning success; only after successful allocation can setup failure reach `tfm_crypto_operation_release(p_handle)` at `secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_cipher.c:196`, `secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_cipher.c:197`, `secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_cipher.c:256`, `secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_cipher.c:258`, `secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_cipher.c:321`, `secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:89`, `secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:90`, `secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:110`, and `secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:112`. Gap: none.
properties.mitigation: Avoid seeding the output handle with caller-controlled iov->op_handle on setup. Initialize the out handle to a known invalid value, track whether allocation actually succeeded and which handle was allocated, and release only that known allocated handle. Alternatively have tfm_crypto_operation_alloc return the handle in a local variable and copy it to out_vec[0] only after successful setup.
properties.reasoning: For setup requests, the code copies the caller-supplied iov->op_handle into out_vec[0] before allocating a new operation, and p_handle remains pointed at that output buffer. If allocation succeeds but psa_cipher_encrypt_setup or psa_cipher_decrypt_setup later fails, control reaches release_operation_and_return, which calls tfm_crypto_operation_release(p_handle). This is safe only if tfm_crypto_operation_alloc always overwrites out_vec[0] with the allocated handle before any later failure and never leaves the caller-supplied value intact. That invariant is not established in this file. If it is violated in some allocation/error configuration, a failed setup could attempt to release an attacker-specified or stale handle, potentially corrupting operation lifetime or freeing another operation slot.
